subject: Observability transition: onboarding checkpoints & logistics
messages:
From: Glen Robertson <glen@cloudhaven.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observability transition: onboarding checkpoints & logistics

Chloe / Laura,

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. We're ready to kick off the observability handoff for our inference platform migration. High-level asks we want to cover in the onboarding: dashboards (SLO/latency, token-cost), tracing hook placement for model-serving, an error taxonomy for inference failures, alert routing + escalation, and a runbook for incident handoffs.

Can your team propose a 2–3 week onboarding cadence and a short checklist of items we should prepare on our side (example logs, service endpoints, access lists)?

I've CC'd ops-eng for any immediate technical questions.

Attachments: none in this initial note.

Thanks,
Glen
Glen Robertson
Director, Platform Ops — CloudHaven

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Glen Robertson <glen@cloudhaven.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability transition: onboarding checkpoints & logistics

Glen — thanks, this is clear and good to scope.

Proposed onboarding cadence (attached as onboarding_cadence.xlsx):
- Week 0 (Kickoff, discovery): 60-min alignment with CloudHaven SREs; confirm data access and retention policy.
- Week 1 (Instrumentation + traces): implement and validate tracing hooks on 2 representative endpoints.
- Week 2 (Dashboards + alerts): deliver baseline dashboards and alert rules; run alert playback.
- Week 3 (Runbook & handoff): finalize runbook, escalation contacts, and 1 tabletop.

Immediate ask from your side:
- A sample of production logs (or redacted snippets) and the standard request trace id format
- List of service endpoints and ingress domains we should instrument
- Contact for on-call escalation and webex access for tabletop

Laura and Ben — can you take ownership of the tracing + alert routing items respectively and add any pre-kickoff checklists?

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments: onboarding_cadence.xlsx (stub)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Glen Robertson <glen@cloudhaven.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-11T14:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability transition: onboarding checkpoints & logistics

Chloe / Glen — adding the runbook template and a short instrumentation checklist. See attached runbook_template.md. Notes:

- Runbook sections: summary, detection signals, triage steps (quick checks), mitigation steps, rollback criteria, postmortem link.
- Tracing hooks: prefer server-side middleware that tags model_id, model_version, request_token_count. For async/cached responses add KV-cache keys to traces.
- Error taxonomy (short): 1) Model decode failure (invalid tokens), 2) Timeout/compute QPS, 3) KV cache miss consistency, 4) Input validation / sanitization errors. Use these labels as alert tags.

Pre-kickoff checklist for CloudHaven:
- Provide a service account with read access to traces/logs and a sample trace id per service.
- Confirm data retention window and whether logs include raw prompts (PII considerations).
- Provide spike window info (expected peak tokens/sec) for batching/caching tuning.

Linking JIRA OPS-7421 for tracking the instrumentation work; I will create subtasks for trace placements.

Laura Bennett
Director, Observability | Redwood Inference
Attachments: runbook_template.md (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Glen Robertson <glen@cloudhaven.com>
Date: 2028-07-12T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability transition: onboarding checkpoints & logistics

Looping in a quick alert-routing proposal before kickoff:

- Alerts grouped by severity: P0 (inference availability / high error-rate), P1 (latency SLO breach), P2 (degraded quality / increased decode errors).
- Routing: P0 -> Platform SRE pager + Redwood on-call; P1 -> On-call + Slack #cloudhaven-ops; P2 -> Email + weekly triage.
- Include automatic fallback policy: if model variant A breaches for >3 mins, route to model variant B and suppress low-priority alerts for 10m.

I attached an alert-routing diagram (alert-routing-diagram.pdf) with escalation windows. Two quick questions for CloudHaven:
1) What escalation window does your paging provider use for P0s (30s, 60s)?
2) Do you want Redwood to own the first responder rotation for the first 30 days?

Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Customer Ops | Redwood Inference
Attachments: alert-routing-diagram.pdf (stub)

From: Glen Robertson <glen@cloudhaven.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-13T15:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability transition: onboarding checkpoints & logistics

Thanks all — this looks good and aligns with our expectations. Confirming:
- Kickoff: 2028-07-18 09:00 PT (60 min)
- We'll provide the sample traces and a service account by EOD 2028-07-14.
- For P0 paging: we use a 60s escalation window; yes, Redwood can own first responder rotation for 30 days.

I also uploaded a redacted log bundle to the drive link you shared (Drive: 1A2b3C4d5E). I'll add OPS-7421 watchers.

Look forward to the kickoff.

Glen Robertson
Director, Platform Ops — CloudHaven
